Monaco :: History :: 19th century :: chunk_0008
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/County_of_nice.svg/250px-County_of_nice.svg.png)](/wiki/File:County_of_nice.svg)

A map of the [County of Nice](/wiki/County_of_Nice "County of Nice") showing the area of the [Italian kingdom of Sardinia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sardinia_(1720%E2%80%931861) "Kingdom of Sardinia (1720–1861)") annexed in 1860 to France (light brown). The area in red had already become part of France before 1860.

In 1793, Revolutionary forces captured Monaco and until 1814 it was occupied by the French (in this period much of Europe had been overrun by the French armies).[[33]](#cite_note-monacoangebote.de-36)[[35]](#cite_note-Monte-carlo.mc-38) The principality was reestablished in 1814 under the Grimaldis. It was designated a protectorate of the [Kingdom of Sardinia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sardinia_(1720%E2%80%931861) "Kingdom of Sardinia (1720–1861)") by the [Congress of Vienna](/wiki/Congress_of_Vienna "Congress of Vienna") in 1815.[[35]](#cite_note-Monte-carlo.mc-38) Monaco remained in this position until 1860 when, by the [Treaty of Turin](/wiki/Treaty_of_Turin_(1860) "Treaty of Turin (1860)"), the Sardinian forces pulled out of the principality; the surrounding [County of Nice](/wiki/County_of_Nice "County of Nice") (as well as [Savoy](/wiki/Savoy "Savoy")) was ceded to France.[[36]](#cite_note-infoplease1-39) Monaco became a French protectorate once again. Italian was the official language in Monaco until 1860, when it was replaced by French.[[37]](#cite_note-miglioverde-40)

Before this time there was unrest in [Menton](/wiki/Menton "Menton") and [Roquebrune](/wiki/Roquebrune-Cap-Martin "Roquebrune-Cap-Martin"), where the townspeople had become weary of heavy taxation by the Grimaldi family. They declared their independence as the [Free Cities of Menton and Roquebrune](/wiki/Free_Cities_of_Menton_and_Roquebrune "Free Cities of Menton and Roquebrune"), hoping for annexation by Sardinia.

[Lionel Messi](/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi"), pictured in 2014, is Barcelona's all-time top scorer, with 672 goals in all competitions.[[1]](#cite_note-Indiv-1)

[Futbol Club Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") is a professional [association football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in [Barcelona](/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), Catalonia, Spain. Founded by a group of footballers led by [Joan Gamper](/wiki/Joan_Gamper "Joan Gamper"), the club has become a symbol of Catalan culture and [Catalanism](/wiki/Catalanism "Catalanism"), hence the motto *"Més que un club"* (More than a club). The official Barça anthem is the "[Cant del Barça](/wiki/Cant_del_Bar%C3%A7a "Cant del Barça")", written by Jaume Picas and [Josep Maria Espinàs](/wiki/Josep_Maria_Espin%C3%A0s "Josep Maria Espinàs").[[2]](#cite_note-2) Unlike many other football clubs, the [*socis*](/wiki/Supporters_of_FC_Barcelona "Supporters of FC Barcelona"), who are the members and supporters of the club, own and operate Barcelona. It is the world's [second richest football club](/wiki/Deloitte_Football_Money_League "Deloitte Football Money League") in terms of revenue, with an annual turnover of €974.8 million in the 2025-26 season.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

[Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") played its first [friendly match](/wiki/Friendly_match "Friendly match") on 8 December 1899 against the English colony in Barcelona in the old velodrome in [Bonanova](/wiki/Bonanova "Bonanova").[[4]](#cite_note-4) Initially, Barcelona played against other local clubs in various [Catalan tournaments](/wiki/Catalan_football_championship "Catalan football championship"). It borders [Delaware](/wiki/Delaware "Delaware") to its southeast, [Maryland](/wiki/Maryland "Maryland") to its south, forming the [Mason-Dixon Line](/wiki/Mason-Dixon_Line "Mason-Dixon Line"), [West Virginia](/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia") to its southwest, [Ohio](/wiki/Ohio "Ohio") to its west, the [Canadian province](/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") of [Ontario](/wiki/Ontario "Ontario") to its northwest via [Lake Erie](/wiki/Lake_Erie "Lake Erie"), [New York](/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") to its north, and the [Delaware River](/wiki/Delaware_River "Delaware River") and [New Jersey](/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") to its east. Pennsylvania is the [fifth-most populous](/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population "List of U.S. states and territories by population") state in the country, with over 13 million residents as of the [2020 United States census](/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). During his lifetime Woodward authored or coauthored almost 200 publications, of which 85 are full papers, the remainder comprising preliminary communications, the text of lectures, and reviews. The pace of his scientific activity soon outstripped his capacity to publish all experimental details, and much of the work in which he participated was not published until a few years after his death. Woodward trained more than two hundred Ph.D. students and postdoctoral workers, many of whom later went on to distinguished careers.

Some of his best-known students include [Robert M. Williams](https://web.archive.org/web/20100718223149/http://rwindigo1.chm.colostate.edu/) (Colorado State), Harry Wasserman (Yale), [Yoshito Kishi](/wiki/Yoshito_Kishi "Yoshito Kishi") (Harvard), [Stuart Schreiber](/wiki/Stuart_Schreiber "Stuart Schreiber") (Harvard), [William R. Roush](/wiki/William_R._Roush "William R. Roush") ([Scripps-Florida](/wiki/Scripps_Research_Institute "Scripps Research Institute")), [Steven A. Benner](/wiki/Steven_Albert_Benner "Steven Albert Benner") (UF), [James D. Wuest](/wiki/James_D._Wuest "James D. Wuest") (Montreal), [Christopher S. Foote](/wiki/Christopher_S._Foote "Christopher S. Foote") (UCLA), [Kendall Houk](/wiki/Kendall_Houk "Kendall Houk") (UCLA), porphyrin chemist Kevin M. Smith (LSU), Thomas R. Hoye (University of Minnesota), [Ronald Breslow](/wiki/Ronald_Breslow "Ronald Breslow") (Columbia University) and [David Dolphin](/wiki/David_Dolphin "David Dolphin") (UBC).

Woodward had an encyclopedic knowledge of chemistry, and an memory for detail.[[16]](#cite_note-Roberts,_J._1990-16) Perhaps the quality that set him most apart from his peers was his exceptional ability to connect disparate threads of knowledge from the chemical literature and apply them effectively to solve chemical problems.[[16]](#cite_note-Roberts,_J._1990-16)

The first time a person landed on the Moon and any extraterrestrial body was when [Neil Armstrong](/wiki/Neil_Armstrong "Neil Armstrong"), the commander of the American mission [Apollo 11](/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11"), set foot on the Moon at 02:56 UTC on July 21, 1969.[[271]](#cite_note-284) Considered the culmination of the [Space Race](/wiki/Space_Race "Space Race"),[[272]](#cite_note-CNN-285) an estimated 500 million people worldwide watched the transmission by the [Apollo TV camera](/wiki/Apollo_TV_camera "Apollo TV camera"), the largest television audience for a live broadcast at that time.[[273]](#cite_note-286)[[274]](#cite_note-287) While at the same time another mission, the robotic sample return mission [Luna 15](/wiki/Luna_15 "Luna 15") by the Soviet Union had been in orbit around the Moon, becoming together with Apollo 11 the first ever case of two extraterrestrial missions being conducted at the same time.

The Apollo missions 11 to 17 (except [Apollo 13](/wiki/Apollo_13 "Apollo 13"), which aborted its planned lunar landing) removed 380.05 kilograms (837.87 lb) of lunar rock and soil in 2,196 [separate samples](/wiki/Moon_rock "Moon rock").[[275]](#cite_note-288)
Scientific instrument packages were installed on the lunar surface during all the Apollo landings. Long-lived [instrument stations](/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Surface_Experiments_Package "Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package"), including heat flow probes, [seismometers](/wiki/Seismometer "Seismometer"), and [magnetometers](/wiki/Magnetometer "Magnetometer"), were installed at the [Apollo 12](/wiki/Apollo_12 "Apollo 12"), [14](/wiki/Apollo_14 "Apollo 14"), [15](/wiki/Apollo_15 "Apollo 15"), [16](/wiki/Apollo_16 "Apollo 16"), and [17](/wiki/Apollo_17 "Apollo 17") landing sites.
